draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Meppadi! This little hill town on the highway between Kozhikode and Ooty runs on tea, and most people here work on the estates, where cardamom grows too.
draft.hungryLine: Look out for Wayanad's bamboo rice, called mulayari locally, plus local Wayanad tea, coffee and home-made chocolates.

moodReplies.show-me-around: The Juma Masjid is a 3 min walk and the CSI Church is 8 min away, and Soochipara Falls and Chembra Peak are among the big sights around Meppadi.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Go for a slow walk through the tea estates and enjoy the cool climate that draws visitors here.
moodReplies.surprise-me: Bamboo only seeds after a very long time, so people say harvesting bamboo rice is a once-in-a-lifetime thing.

tips.title: Walk the tea estates.
tips.body: Tea is Meppadi's main work, and walking the estates and hiking the hills is the way to see Wayanad.

tips.title: Be kind and mindful.
tips.body: Meppadi was one of the Wayanad villages worst hit by deadly landslides in July 2024, so tread gently.

story.title: A tea town
story.body: Tea cultivation became the main work in Meppadi, and most people here work on tea estates where they grow cardamom too.

story.title: The landslides
story.body: Meppadi was one of the villages in Wayanad district most affected by deadly landslides in July 2024.

story.title: Hill town stop
story.body: Visitors still come for the climate, with Soochipara Falls, Chembra Peak and Meenmutty Falls among the attractions around.
